title: Pellet Smoked Chicken Quarters
seoTitle: Pellet Smoked Chicken Quarters | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Crisp-skinned leg quarters with BBQ rub for ten
subtitle: Crisp-skinned leg quarters with BBQ rub for ten
description: Chicken leg quarters are dry-brined, rubbed with a sweet-spice BBQ blend, and smoked on a pellet grill until skin crisps and dark meat hits 175°F. Finish with a light glaze and serve with corn and beans.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Pellet Smoked Chicken Quarters in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Dry-brine the quarters
steps.instruction: Pat quarters dry and season all sides with kosher salt. Refrigerate uncovered on a wire rack 2–24 hours so skin dries and seasons deeply.

steps.title: Apply BBQ rub
steps.instruction: Mix brown sugar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and chili powder. Coat quarters evenly, pressing rub into skin and under loosened skin where possible.

steps.title: Smoke until nearly done
steps.instruction: Heat pellet smoker to 275°F. Smoke quarters skin-side up until thickest part of thigh hits 170°F and skin begins to tighten, about 55–65 minutes. Target oven/smoker temperature: 275°F.

steps.title: Glaze and crisp
steps.instruction: Brush with BBQ sauce and raise smoker temp to 375°F for 10 minutes until glaze sets and skin crisps. Verify 175°F internal in the thigh before pulling. Target oven/smoker temperature: 375°F.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Pellet Smoked Chicken Quarters onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 10 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Rest and plate
steps.instruction: Rest quarters 5 minutes. Serve two per person with warm baked beans and cornbread. Keep extra sauce at the line for second passes.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Pellet Smoked Chicken Quarters — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: 175°F in the thigh is the target—legs stay juicy while breast-only cuts would be dry at that temp.
Pat quarters dry right before smoking even after dry-brining—surface moisture kills crisp skin.
Spatchcock quarters if you need faster cooks on a night with early tones.
tonightSpread: Smoked leg quarters with baked beans, cornbread, and dill pickles.
Simple iceberg salad with ranch for crews wanting something cold alongside smoky chicken.
leftovers: Pull meat and mix into smoky chicken salad with celery and mayo.
Shred and simmer in white beans for a fast smoked chicken chili.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Leg quarters are cheap, hard to overcook, and eat like a feast. Pellet smokers make temperature control easy on busy shift days when nobody can babysit a fire.
mealPrepNotes: Dry-brine quarters uncovered on a rack in the walk-in for up to 24 hours for crispier skin. Rub can be applied hours ahead. Quarters hold well wrapped at 170°F for 45 minutes.
